To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the total amount of H2O in the Earth’s exosphere is ~1.4 × 1021 kilograms (kg), and in the geosphere is ~2.4 × 10−4 × 1.4 ×1021 kg.
the amount of total water in the geosphere is comparable to the total amount of ocean water, and that water is a dynamic and mobile element in the Earth’s interior.
the Earth’s geohydrologic system is a dynamic, interconnected, and interdependent system, and that it includes all reservoirs and fluxes of water on Earth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the occurrence and movement, or cycling, of water in and around the Earth.
the distribution of water in Earth’s exosphere and geospheres.
the distribution and cycling of water in the solid Earth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many uncertainties in the distribution of water in Earth’s geohydrologic system.
the water in the oceans is not the same water as the water in the atmosphere or in the rivers, lakes, glaciers, or groundwater.
water on Earth is ubiquitous, but its occurrence in the various reservoir systems of the geohydrolcic cycle has not been well characterized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Earth has an active water cycle that involves both the atmosphere and the solid Earth.

the water cycle is the movement of water on, in, and above the Earth, the water cycle describes the continuous movement of water within the land, atmosphere, and biota; liquid water makes up only 0.01% of Earth’s water, a larger percentage exists as groundwater, ice, saltwater, and atmospheric water, and a very small fraction of Earth’s water (0.0001%) is fresh water.
the water in the Earth is distributed in a complex system, with a wide range of reservoirs that have varying amounts of water and different residence times.
The main takeaway from our work is that
water is a dynamic, ubiquitous, mobile, and reactive constituent of Earth’s interior and surface.
the Earth is not a water planet, as is commonly assumed.
the amount of H2O in the Earth’s interior is comparable to that of the oceans.
